title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Unit-of-Analysis, Fragmentation and Dependency Collapse
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — единица анализа, фрагментация и схлопывание зависимостей

scan_scope: selected manifests, historical snapshots, receipts and supersession records

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS_DEPENDENCY
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: The dependence created when multiple archive objects are fragments, snapshots, receipts, derivatives, supersessions, or differently formatted views of a smaller number of underlying source events or claims.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: How many independent underlying events exist after collapsing derivative artifacts that represent the same lineage or source event?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_eighth_order: The candidate sits above source-level residual structure: even after removing interpretive metadata, the apparent multiplicity of sources may still be inflated by the archive's chosen unit of storage.

emergent_invariants.name: FILE_COUNT_IS_NOT_SOURCE_COUNT
emergent_invariants.description: Multiple JSON objects can encode the same underlying event, snapshot, proof state, interpretation, or source lineage. Connection recurrence must therefore operate on dependency-collapsed source units as well as raw files.

emergent_invariants.name: DERIVATIVE_ARTIFACT_AMPLIFICATION
emergent_invariants.description: A single underlying event can generate a manifest, hash receipt, report, proof capsule, index entry and audit receipt. Counting each as a separate witness inflates apparent support.

emergent_invariants.name: SUPERCESSION_IS_NOT_REPLICATION
emergent_invariants.description: Sequential revisions can improve, correct, or reinterpret the same underlying object. Version multiplicity must not be mistaken for independent replication.

emergent_invariants.name: FRAGMENTATION_CAN_CREATE_FALSE_CROSS_DOMAIN_LINKS
emergent_invariants.description: When one research episode is split across technical, audit, proof, and symbolic folders, JANUS may rediscover the same lineage as if it were a cross-domain connection.

emergent_invariants.name: DEPENDENCY_COLLAPSE_CHANGES_GRAPH_DENSITY
emergent_invariants.description: The graph of connections can become substantially sparser when derivative and shared-lineage objects are collapsed into underlying source units. The change in density is itself a diagnostic signal.

connections.machine_observation: The registry contains source objects, derived proofs, receipts, indexes, hashes, reports and historical snapshots that may refer to the same underlying research episode.
connections.pattern_description: Before asking whether two files are independent, JANUS should ask whether they are even two distinct source events.
connections.why_non_obvious: Git treats every file as a separate object, while epistemic independence is defined over underlying events, observations, or claims rather than file boundaries.
alternative_explanations: The registry may already encode dependency through explicit provenance fields in individual records.
Some receipts intentionally provide independent evidence even when they reference the same source event.
connections.falsification_route: Build a lineage-aware source graph and compare raw file-level recurrence against event-collapsed recurrence.

connections.machine_observation: The same research lines can produce manifests, proof capsules, hashes, audit records, merge receipts, reports and index entries.
connections.pattern_description: One source event can fan out into many machine-readable artifacts, each of which may later participate in Connection discovery.
connections.why_non_obvious: Each derivative carries real provenance and may be individually useful, creating a temptation to count provenance richness as observational multiplicity.
alternative_explanations: Some derivative artifacts may add genuinely new observations rather than only restating an old one.
A receipt can be operationally independent even when its subject is not independent.
connections.falsification_route: Classify each artifact as source, derivative, validator, witness, or metadata-only and recompute Connection counts using only eligible independent source classes.

connections.machine_observation: The archive explicitly preserves historical snapshots while distinguishing them from current authority.
connections.pattern_description: Historical versions form a dependency chain, not a set of independent observations. A connection repeated across versions may be evidence of persistence or simply persistence of the same source lineage.
connections.why_non_obvious: Version history is often visually presented as many records even when all versions derive from one evolving object.
alternative_explanations: A later version may introduce genuinely new empirical evidence.
Supersession metadata may already prevent naive counting if the detector consumes it correctly.
connections.falsification_route: Collapse supersession chains and compare connection recurrence before and after version collapsing, while separately counting newly introduced evidence.

connections.machine_observation: The same research program can be distributed across technical, proof, audit and portfolio layers.
connections.pattern_description: Cross-folder recurrence may partly reflect deliberate decomposition of one research lineage into separate governance and evidence layers rather than a true cross-domain discovery.
connections.why_non_obvious: The directory structure makes related artifacts appear spatially separated even when provenance links them tightly.
alternative_explanations: The directory split can be a genuine architectural separation of functions.
Some cross-folder relations may survive complete lineage collapsing and therefore remain meaningful.
connections.falsification_route: Cluster by underlying research episode before graph construction and compare cross-domain connection counts with and without lineage collapsing.

connections.machine_observation: Connection recurrence is currently described primarily at the file/object level, while previous scans already identify shared provenance, recursive memory, authority, representation and order as dependency layers.
connections.pattern_description: The change in graph density after collapsing dependent nodes may itself become a diagnostic measure of how much of the apparent relational structure is generated by the archive rather than by underlying source diversity.
connections.why_non_obvious: A lower edge count after collapsing dependencies is not automatically evidence of a weaker archive; it may be evidence of a better-calibrated unit of analysis.
alternative_explanations: Over-collapsing can destroy legitimate independent observations that happen to share provenance.
A sparse graph can simply reflect an overly aggressive dependency model.
connections.falsification_route: Report raw graph, dependency-collapsed graph and partially collapsed graphs together, with explicit sensitivity analysis over lineage-collapse rules.

eighth_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: UNDERLYING_EVENT -> {RAW_SOURCE, DERIVATIVES, SNAPSHOTS, RECEIPTS} -> LINEAGE_COLLAPSE -> REMOVE_META_DEPENDENCIES -> RESIDUAL_CONNECTION
eighth_order_graph.critical_prediction: Some high-frequency connections will materially weaken after derivative artifacts and supersession chains are collapsed into underlying source events.
eighth_order_graph.counter_prediction: Connections that remain stable across lineage collapsing, dependency removal and representation swaps are stronger candidates for genuine source-level structure.

next_scan_strategy.name: UNIT_OF_ANALYSIS_BENCHMARK
next_scan_strategy.target: Determine the appropriate independence unit for every high-value Connection candidate.
tests: EVENT_COLLAPSE: map files to underlying research episodes or source events.
DERIVATIVE_COLLAPSE: exclude hashes, receipts, manifests and index-only derivatives from independent-source counts.
SUPERSESSION_COLLAPSE: collapse version chains while separately retaining newly introduced evidence.
LINEAGE_COLLAPSE: group records sharing a research origin before computing recurrence.
WITNESS_ROLE_AUDIT: distinguish source, validator, witness and metadata roles.
CROSS_UNIT_RECOMPUTATION: compare file-level, artifact-level and event-level graphs.
RESIDUAL_EDGE_TEST: run the surviving candidates through the previous context-removal battery.
EXTERNAL_REPLICATION: where applicable, reproduce only the event-level claim outside the Meta Registry.
next_scan_strategy.promotion_rule: Do not promote a connection because it spans many files. Promotion requires evidence that the edge survives dependency collapse at the appropriate underlying source unit.

limitations: This scan identifies a structural risk in the archive model; it does not yet quantify the degree of fragmentation inflation.
Some derivative artifacts can contain genuinely independent checks and must not be collapsed automatically.
The correct independence unit can differ by connection type: event, experiment, document, witness, or external source may be appropriate in different cases.
No connection in this scan establishes scientific novelty, causation, or truth.
canonical_rule: Before counting a relationship, determine what the independent thing actually is. A repository object is a storage unit; it is not automatically an independent source of evidence.
